← All features

Tee sheet and online booking.

Every booking on one sheet, and a booking page in your course's own look.

Every booking on one sheet.

Online, phone and walk-in bookings land on the same sheet. The top line shows players booked, groups on the course, who has checked in, what is paid and what isn't yet. Each group's color says whether it has paid.

A booking page in your colors.

Golfers pick a day, their players, holes and walking or riding, and see only the times that fit. You choose a light or dark page and an outline color, and link it from your own website.

Golfers hear when a time opens.

When a day is full, a golfer can ask to be emailed, or texted if they agree, the moment a time opens. The first golfer to book gets it, and nothing is held.

Try it.

A golfer books 1:10 PM for two players on your booking page. Press Book and watch the group land on the real tee sheet.

1:10 PM · 18 holes · 2 playersOnline booking, pay at the course

Not booked yet. The 1:10 PM row is open.

← All features

Payments.

Golfers pay online, at the counter or on their own phone, into your own Stripe account.

Paid on their own phone.

Text a group a pay link and each golfer checks in and pays on their own phone. They see every line, including the booking fee, before they pay.

Your policy, shown before they book.

Golfers see your cancellation policy in plain words and tick a box to agree before they book. When your policy has late-cancel or no-show fees, golfers save a card when they book, so the fee is covered.

At the counter, too.

Staff open a group on the tee sheet to check it in. Payment at the counter can be cash, a Stripe card reader or a pay link texted to the golfer.

Every payment in one place.

Revenue lists every payment by day, with your payouts, the ledger and cancellations beside it.

What it costs.

No setup fee, no monthly fee, no commission on your green fees.

  • Golfers pay $1.50 per player on each online booking, added to your price.
  • Membership dues collected through GreenReserve carry 1% of the dues (and any initiation fee), added to what the member pays.
  • Pro-shop items paid by card carry a GreenReserve service fee of 1% of the items; cash carries none.
  • Your green fee and our fee are collected in one card payment to your own Stripe account; our $1.50 per player is then passed to GreenReserve.
  • Stripe's standard card-processing fee applies to the payment, the same as any card you take today. GreenReserve charges you nothing on top of it.

Pro shop and range.

A register for walk-up sales, with stock counts and a daily close-out, on the same system as your tee sheet.

Ring it up at the register.

Tap items to build a sale, add a discount if you need one, and charge it. Take cash, use a Stripe card reader or text the customer a pay link.

Know what's on the shelf.

Count stock if you want to. Add new stock with what it cost you, and set a number to get an email when an item runs low.

Close out the drawer.

At the end of the day, count the drawer by bill and coin. You see what should be in it and the difference, and card sales are listed for reference.

Range balls with the round.

Golfers can add a range bucket when they book, at the prices you set. The same buckets sell at the register.

← All features

Memberships and log-in.

Your memberships, members and residents, with a log-in on your booking page.

Every membership in one list.

Set up each membership with its price, its rates and how far ahead members can book. Residents get the resident rate once you add them.

Who has paid, and who hasn't.

Each membership lists its members, whether their dues are paid and through when. Remind everyone who is overdue in one step.

Members log in on your booking page.

Members and residents log in with their email and a 6-digit code. Everyone else books as a guest, with no account.

They see their own rates.

Once logged in, every tee time shows their price beside the public one, and the days their longer booking window opens.

Events.

Tournaments, leagues and outings, held on your tee sheet, with sign-up and entry fees.

Every event on one page.

See what's coming up, how many players have signed up, what's owed and what is still to do.

Set up step by step.

Each event holds its tee times, sets the price per player and what's included, and walks you through a checklist until it's ready.

Golfers sign up online.

Open sign-up and golfers enter themselves and their group from the event's own page.

Analytics and the AI assistant.

How your course is doing, in plain words, and an assistant that knows your day.

See where the empty times are.

Your busiest and quietest hours, the spots that went unsold and what they were worth, and where the next 30 days are heading.

A written review every month.

At the start of every month you get a written review of the month before, built only from your own numbers.

An assistant that knows your course.

Ask who's still to check in or how last week went, and it answers from your own tee sheet. It can draft a change, like a pay link, and nothing happens until you confirm it.

Team and permissions.

A log-in for each person on your staff, and what each one can do.

Everyone in one place.

Invite your staff and put each person in a role. You see when each person was last active.

Roles you set.

Each role says what it can do, area by area: the tee sheet, payments, the pro shop, members and events, reports and settings.

Change one person, not the role.

Open a person to change any area for just them. Areas that move money are marked.
